PullRequest.Title: Harden content exclusion failrue condition
PullRequest.Body:

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The new test pins the per-file call count, and the complete call path to Git/filesystem operations and high-cardinality production callers is explicit. Only whether a given local-only repo is already open determines how much filesystem I/O accompanies each call.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Git extension API calls and, on the unopened-repository path, filesystem stat/open/read operations for .git/config.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: O(F×R) lookups for F distinct files plus repeated evaluations R while the repository has no remote, instead of O(1) repository resolution followed by cache hits. Search filtering runs up to 20 checks concurrently, so the repeated calls also burst at that concurrency.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Excessive Git/filesystem I/O, higher CPU, and substantially increased bulk-search/index latency.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Resolved RepoMetadata was cached by repository root regardless of remote count, so later files under a local-only repository skipped getRepositoryFetchUrls and each settled file verdict could be memoized.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: A successfully resolved repository with no fetch remote is deliberately omitted from _repoRootCache, and negative file verdicts for it are also left unsettled, so every file check resolves the same repository through Git again.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT lines 326-327 newly refuse to cache metadata when fetchUrls.length===0; before the PR each resolved repoMetadata was inserted directly into _repoRootCache.
Findings.Title: Bound empty-remote repository revalidation per repository
Findings.Impact: A newly initialized or intentionally local-only repository subjected to a bulk file search/index now performs one Git repository lookup per returned file; repeated checks of the same file also miss the verdict cache. For an unopened repository each lookup can additionally stat the path, ask Git for its root, and read .git/config. Whole-workspace indexing can reach 100,000 files or all files, causing severe I/O/API fan-out and startup delay.
Findings.Evidence: Line 326 makes cacheRepoMetadata return for an empty fetchUrls list. isIgnored calls getRepositoryFetchUrls on every _repoRootCache miss, while repoSettled=false also prevents negative verdict memoization. The production Git implementation may perform workspace.fs.stat, getRepositoryRoot, and workspace.fs.readFile(.git/config). Tests added by this PR explicitly assert two calls for two files in a no-remote repo, and workspace indexing enumerates up to 100,000/all files.
Findings.Recommendation: Negative-cache/coalesce the empty-remote resolution by repository root with a short expiry or invalidate it from a repository/remote-state event. This preserves eventual remote discovery while bounding Git resolution to once per repository per refresh interval instead of once per file.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The removed guard and eager O(N) helper are explicit, as are production cardinalities. Only exact duration varies by workspace.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Promise, closure, and array allocations plus repeated enablement/cache/glob-check CPU work.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: O(N) extra work for N provider results; realistic N reaches 100,000 files, while external reconciliation can request every file.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased indexing latency, CPU usage, allocation, and GC pressure.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The method returned provider results directly whenever isRegexExclusionsEnabled was false, avoiding per-resource promises and duplicate rule evaluation.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: findFiles now post-filters every provider result through isCopilotIgnored even when exclusion is disabled or all loaded rules are globs already passed to the provider.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 43 replaces the previous conditional no-regex return with unconditional filterIngoredResources; the same change exists in findFilesWithDefaultExcludes.
Findings.Title: Preserve the no-regex fast path for file searches
Findings.Impact: Large workspace enumeration now allocates and awaits one queued promise per file and builds additional arrays. With the 100,000-file local-index default, this adds startup CPU, GC pressure, and latency without changing results in disabled or glob-only configurations.
Findings.Evidence: Line 43 unconditionally calls filterIngoredResources after the exclusion glob was supplied to super.findFiles. That helper eagerly maps the entire array into Limiter jobs and Promise.all. The removed pre-diff guard returned results when !isRegexExclusionsEnabled; workspace indexing uses the same search service at high cardinality.
Findings.Recommendation: After rules are loaded and globs are passed to the provider, return directly when !isRegexExclusionsEnabled; reserve per-resource post-filtering for content/regex rules.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed ordering and both timeout constants are explicit, and the extension activation-failure/null-service paths that never settle the observable are directly implemented. Only the prevalence of those environments is uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Wall-clock time waiting on Git extension initialization/discovery and pending search requests.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The delay is a fixed 30 seconds on the cold unavailable-Git path; it is shared rather than multiplied by callers, but it blocks every concurrent exclusion-dependent search during that interval.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Blocked search critical path and cold-search timeout.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The method immediately read the current Git API and returned undefined when the extension/API was unavailable, so content-exclusion checks were not blocked on Git initialization.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every getRepositoryFetchUrls call now waits for global initial Git discovery before it can return, with a shared 30-second timeout when discovery never settles.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 202 newly executes await this.waitForInitialDiscovery() before the prior immediate API availability check; the same diff defines that wait with a 30,000 ms timeout.
Findings.Title: Avoid waiting 30 seconds when Git discovery is unavailable
Findings.Impact: With content exclusion enabled and vscode.git missing or activation failing, the first file or text search blocks in its first exclusion check for the full 30 seconds. The Copilot text-search tool has a 20-second timeout, so that cold search times out before this wait completes; concurrent callers all wait on the same promise.
Findings.Evidence: The added await at line 202 precedes even getExtensionApi(). waitForInitialDiscovery uses INITIAL_DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT_MS=30,000 and only resolves earlier when _isInitialized changes. GitExtensionServiceImpl returns from a failed activate() without firing onDidChange, and NullGitExtensionService exposes Event.None, so those supported unavailable/failure paths leave _isInitialized false. findTextInFilesTool independently times searches out after 20,000 ms.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep pending discovery off the search critical path: when the Git API is unavailable/pending, return an unsettled result that RemoteContentExclusion does not memoize (it already gates negative caching on initialization), or explicitly settle immediately for unavailable/failed activation. Do not use a 30-second wait that exceeds the caller's timeout.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: Sequential control flow and the transitive filesystem boundary are explicit, as are realistic result caps. The exact delay depends on cache warmth and filesystem latency, which affects severity rather than mechanism confidence.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Filesystem open/read/close operations and SHA-256 computation for each cold unique matching file.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cold cost grows linearly with the number of unique result URIs (cached repeat matches in the same file are cheap), with effective filesystem concurrency fixed at 1 despite RemoteContentExclusion's file-read limiter allowing 10.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Reduced streaming throughput, delayed first/subsequent results, and search timeout risk.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: findTextInFiles2 directly returned the provider stream and did not insert per-result work into its critical path. The existing non-streaming exclusion paths either batch checks or use limiters with greater concurrency.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new streamed text-search wrapper awaits isCopilotIgnored inline before requesting and yielding the next result, making all exclusion checks effectively single-threaded.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 103 introduces an awaited exclusion check inside the sequential async-generator loop; no such work existed in the previous findTextInFiles2 path.
Findings.Title: Pipeline content checks for streamed text results
Findings.Impact: When content regex rules are loaded, the first result for each matching file opens, reads up to 1 KiB, and closes that file before the stream advances. The find-text tool can request up to 1,001 grep-style results, so a broad search across distinct files serializes hundreds of filesystem operations and can consume its 20-second timeout, especially on remote filesystems.
Findings.Evidence: Line 103 awaits each isCopilotIgnored inside a for-await loop. RemoteContentExclusion routes content rules through readFileFromTextBufferOrFS, which opens, reads, and closes the file and then hashes it. The tool caps ordinary results at 200 but grep mode requests 5× that plus one; all work is on the collection critical path.
Findings.Recommendation: Use a small bounded look-ahead pipeline for exclusion checks (reusing a limiter near the existing 10/20 limits), preserve provider order when yielding, and cancel queued work once maxResults or the caller token is reached.

Scenarios.Scenario: First content-exclusion decision or Copilot search during extension startup
Scenarios.CriticalPath: isCopilotIgnored reaches RemoteContentExclusion.isIgnored, which reaches getRepositoryFetchUrls; the added initial-discovery wait must complete before repository lookup, rule loading, and a verdict. This blocks file and text search progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Wait for and query the vscode.git extension API for repository/remotes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shared discovery wait, then one lookup per uncached repository/file depending on repository-root caching.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The method checked getExtensionApi immediately and returned undefined without waiting.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The new wait precedes the API availability check and blocks the first exclusion-dependent search.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch repository and organization content-exclusion rules from CAPI.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cold cache: one coalesced/batched fetch per required repository/global-rule key; warm TTL cache: zero.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Cold uncached verdicts already fetched rules and warm verdicts reused them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A cold verdict waits for only its required repository keys; this boundary already existed and remains downstream of the new Git wait.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One cold Git-discovery state shared by all concurrent file checks; result cardinality does not multiply the 30-second wait because the promise is shared.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All concurrent callers coalesce on _initialDiscoverySettled, but they are all blocked until initialization or the fixed timeout. Later warm calls skip the wait once initialized.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold pending/unavailable Git takes the wait; initialized Git is a warm fast path. Remote rules are fetched on cache miss and reused by TTL; unsettled repository verdicts are intentionally not negatively cached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: changed ordering, non-settling activation/null paths, and both timeout constants are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Git activation failure or unavailable-Git prevalence varies, but the 30-second delay and the search tool's 20-second budget are fixed.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: the added discovery wait can exceed the entire search budget before checking that Git is unavailable.

Scenarios.Scenario: Whole-workspace file enumeration for local/external indexing
Scenarios.CriticalPath: findFilesWithDefaultExcludes obtains exclusion globs, runs the provider search, then now post-filters every returned URI before the index can process any results.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider search per workspace-folder/index request, returning up to 100,000 or all matching files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same search ran, but non-regex configurations returned its results directly.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing provider boundary supplies the collection; the diff adds an O(N) post-processing barrier before callers receive it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve a file to a Git repository and enumerate remotes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one cold lookup per cached repository; after the diff, one per file and repeated evaluation for repositories with zero remotes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Resolved empty-remote repository metadata was cached by root, bounding lookup count to one per repository.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each cache miss is awaited by one of 20 filtering workers, delaying completion of the full post-filter barrier.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: For unopened repositories, stat the URI, resolve the Git root, and read .git/config.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: After the empty-remote cache change, potentially once per returned file in that repository; otherwise once per cold repository resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The first resolved repository metadata served subsequent files under that root.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs inside each awaited exclusion check and can dominate large local-only workspace enumeration.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Coalesced and batched on cold misses; zero on warm TTL hits. Empty-remote repositories require only the global key, but Git resolution still repeats.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same rule-fetch cache and batching path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold batches are awaited; unchanged batching prevents per-file network fan-out.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Returned workspace files: default local index up to 100,000; external reconciliation requests Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER and therefore effectively all files.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: filterIngoredResources eagerly queues every result, limits checks to 20, and awaits Promise.all. Downstream workspace index checks can add another limiter, but the new filter must fully complete first.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Provider-side globs already remove glob-excluded paths. With no regex rules the former fast path avoided all post-checks. Repository/rule/verdict caches make warm checks cheaper, except empty-remote repositories are now deliberately excluded from repository and negative-verdict caches.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: removed no-regex guard, eager Promise mapping, no-remote test call counts, and production callers are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact CPU/GC and Git API duration depend on workspace size and whether the repository is already open; the 100,000/all-file cardinality and per-file mechanisms are established.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable twice: unconditional no-regex post-filtering adds redundant O(N) allocation/CPU, and empty-remote cache refusal adds per-file Git/filesystem work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Streamed find-text tool search with content regex exclusions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The provider stream starts only after minimatch rules load; each result then awaits isCopilotIgnored before it can be yielded or the next provider result consumed. The tool collects the stream and awaits completion within 20 seconds.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stream workspace text-search results from vscode.workspace.findTextInFiles2.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider search; the PR removes the provider max and cancels after the filtered allowed-result quota, so scanned hits depend on excluded-hit prevalence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The provider stream was returned directly with its own maxResults.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Provider results feed the sequential exclusion loop; search progress cannot outrun each check.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open, read up to 1 KiB, and close each cold file, with file-system-service fallback for non-file/failed local reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per cold unique matching URI under regex rules; cached repeated matches in the same file do not reread.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: findTextInFiles2 did not perform exclusion file reads on the result stream.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Introduced into the stream at effective concurrency 1, delaying every subsequent result.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cold repository/global keys are batched/coalesced; warm cache makes zero calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Rule loading existed for other exclusion paths, but findTextInFiles2 did not consume it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before content checks; unchanged rule caching bounds network calls.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cold unique matching files, not raw match count after URI verdict caching; grep mode can request up to 1,001 results from a 200-result cap multiplied by five plus one.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The async-generator loop makes exclusion checks and transitive file reads concurrency 1, despite the file-read limiter allowing 10. Search cancellation occurs after enough allowed results are yielded.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm per-URI verdicts avoid rereads until rule expiry/generation changes. Cold unique files under content rules read and hash once; CAPI rules are TTL-cached and repository requests are coalesced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: inline await, file open/read/close implementation, tool limits, and 20-second budget are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Local SSD reads may be cheap, while remote/fallback filesystem reads can be much slower; the serial control flow and up-to-1,001 unique-file bound are certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: required enforcement is placed in a serial loop rather than a bounded order-preserving pipeline.

Scenarios.Scenario: Initial and retrying scan for local .copilotignore files
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The first enabled isCopilotIgnored/asMinimatchPattern now awaits init; init searches each file-scheme workspace folder for .copilotignore and reads discovered files before returning a verdict.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Search each workspace folder for .copilotignore and read each result.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One search per file-scheme workspace folder on cold init; one read per found ignore file. Persistent failures can repeat the scan no more than once per five seconds of active checks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: isCopilotIgnored did not await init, so this scan was not guaranteed on that decision path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Newly awaited by first enabled decisions, but shared across callers and necessary to avoid startup answers before local policy loads.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Workspace-folder count and discovered .copilotignore file count; on persistent failure, at most one rescan is initiated after each five-second interval when another enforcement call arrives.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Workspace folders are scanned sequentially; concurrent callers share one _init promise. Failed scans are rate-limited by the five-second timestamp.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Successful initialization is cached for the service lifetime. A failed scan is cached for five seconds then the whole folder scan is retried; successful rule files remain tracked.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: call path and sharing/retry state are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Folder count, remote workspace latency, and failure persistence vary; coalescing and five-second retry bound limit amplification.
Scenarios.Verdict: Not separately reportable: the new cold scan is shared, bounded, and directly required for policy enforcement; retries are rate-limited rather than per-result.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 13 changed files and every diff hunk. Submitted four findings covering the unavailable-Git startup stall, redundant no-regex bulk filtering, empty-remote repository cache loss, and serialized content-rule file reads. Checked startup/local-ignore initialization, bulk indexing, streamed text search, CAPI caching/batching, Git/filesystem boundaries, cancellation, and effective concurrency.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
